task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: teammate gain in absent player's primary play types
methodological_questions: Can the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile be shown to be the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types?
How many absence spells and independent cases are needed to test a nearest-profile teammate ranking?
Do the play-by-play-derived initiation records give stable enough pre-absence profiles to define 'closest'?
How should spells be clustered, since 148 spells come from only 11 cases?
evidence_establishes: The retrieval returned no records, so no earlier study by this project on this question or on related absence, usage-redistribution, or profile-matching designs is available in this setting.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the nearest-profile teammate is the largest gainer is not established by any retrieved record.
No prior effect size, variance estimate, or validated pipeline for play-type initiation records is available.
Nothing shows whether the 11-case design supports a ranking test.
own_inferences: The unit of inference is the case (player absence), not the spell. The 148 spells are repeated observations nested within 11 cases, so the effective sample is about 11, which is far too small for a ranking test of a single top-ranked teammate across several play types.

Defining 'closest' three different ways (initiation profile, minutes, same-position minutes) creates analytic flexibility. Without a single pre-specified metric, a positive result could be selected post hoc.
Pre-absence profiles built from derived play-type records may be contaminated if the absence itself or injury-related minute changes are visible in the profile window.
A positive finding could reflect that the closest-profile teammate also absorbs the most minutes or the most possessions overall, not play-type-specific reorganization.
uncertainties: The exact definition of 'primary types' and how many play types qualify is not stated.

The 2025-26 regular season and playoffs are partial before 2026-04-13 and 2026-06-21, so any analysis run on the stated 2026-11-01 date would use an incomplete 2025-26 window. This creates DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY risk and a possible mismatch between pre- and post-absence windows.
How spells map onto absences (overlapping, repeated, or truncated) and how cases were defined is not described.
The reliability of [source]-database play-type labels (initiator attribution, play-type assignment) has not been validated in any retrieved record.
Whether the 11 cases span enough player roles to support any generalization is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieval returned no records, so no prior result, failed approach, or validated design changed the decision. The decision rests only on the stated data structure (11 cases, 148 spells, partial 2025-26 window, derived labels) and general methodological reasoning.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 11 independent cases are available. A ranking test that the nearest-profile teammate is the largest gainer cannot reach useful power with this count, even with 148 spells.
The pre-absence initiation profile depends on derived play-type labels whose reliability is not validated, and profile similarity across few games per player is noisy.
The 2025-26 window is partial at the stated date, so pre- and post-absence windows may be incomplete or inconsistent.

prior_work.summary: No prior work was retrieved (empty result), so whether this question has already been answered by earlier project studies is unknown. No identifiers are cited.

risks.text: 11 cases give very low power for a ranking claim; spell-level counts inflate apparent n.
Play-type initiation counts per teammate per absence may be very small, so profiles and gains are unstable.
Initiation profiles and play-type labels derived from play-by-play are not validated for reliability across games or seasons.
Players selected because of notable absences or unusual pre-absence usage are likely to show regression toward baseline; the largest gainer may reflect reversion rather than profile similarity.
Play-type and initiator attribution from play-by-play may misassign possessions, which shifts both the profile and the gain measure.
Minutes, position, starter status, and team-level pace or injuries may drive both profile similarity and usage gain; the 'most minutes' version is also a confounded alternative.
Three competing definitions of closeness across multiple play types create many comparisons with no pre-specified primary.
If profiles or minute baselines are computed using any window that includes post-absence games, the ranking is contaminated.
Partial 2025-26 data and changing league play-type usage across 2022-23 to 2025-26 can confound pre/post comparisons.
The gain measure is derived from the same play-by-play used to define primary types, so the outcome and selection may be entangled.

design.estimand: As posed, the nearest-profile teammate's gain in the absent player's primary play types, relative to other teammates. Given the data, the minimum viable estimand is descriptive: the within-case rank of profile similarity against play-type gain, reported with uncertainty, not a confirmatory ranking claim.
design.unit: Absence case (player-absence event), with spells nested within cases. Teammates are the comparison units within each case.
design.sample: 11 cases, 148 spells, drawn from 2022-23 to 2024-25 full seasons plus 2025-26 regular season only after 2026-04-13. Playoffs excluded unless complete. The 2025-26 window is excluded if it is incomplete at analysis time.
design.power: Not achievable for a confirmatory ranking test with 11 cases. Any reported power must be computed from a pre-specified effect size and the case-level variance, which is not available from retrieval; do not claim adequate power.
design.controls: Pre-absence minutes, position, starter status, team pace, and game-count exposure as covariates or matching variables. Profile windows must end before the absence begins. Use a leave-one-case-out or case-clustered analysis.
design.falsification: A placebo test: apply the same nearest-profile ranking to non-absence periods or to non-primary play types. If the closest-profile teammate also ranks top there, the effect is not specific to absence. Also compare against the most-minutes and same-position alternatives.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one primary closeness metric (the initiation-profile distance) and one primary play-type set. Treat minutes and same-position rules as secondary with a correction across them.
design.decision_rule: Only a descriptive report is warranted now. Claim support only if the nearest-profile teammate ranks first in the largest-gain set across most cases, survives the placebo test, and holds under the minutes-based control. Otherwise report as inconclusive. Do not state a rejection from 11 cases.
design.data_version: Freeze the data version on a fixed date; use only complete seasons (2022-23 to 2024-25 and complete 2025-26 regular season) and exclude partial 2025-26 playoffs. Record the play-by-play and graph-database build version.
